summary: T42 attempt 3: the full verification matrix was re-run independently on the working tree with Node v26.5.0. GATE PASS. Twenty checks: 19 PASS, 1 WARN (advisory health adapter, exit 0, 0 P0/P1, 7 P2 complexity), 0 FAIL. pnpm test was green in 6 of 6 complete workspace executions (137 tests; apps/cli 18 files / 92 tests), three of them under deliberate CPU oversubscription of 16, 24 and 48 spinner workers on a 10-core machine. T42-F-001 is shown closed by mechanism, not merely absent: under 24- and 48-worker load, five individual tests in apps/cli/src/runtime/inbound.test.ts exceeded the old 5000ms vitest default (5184, 5439, 5164, 5280, 6743 ms) and the runs stayed green because T43's testTimeout 30000 absorbed them; before T43 each would have been a failure. The T43-N-001 look-alike (Timeout calling onTaskUpdate) occurred 0 times; load was deliberately kept below the ~30x oversubscription level at which T43 recorded it. T45/T46 confirmed at the binary level against a real relay binary and real dist/cli.js: first publish claimable=true, repeat-while-unclaimed claimable=true with identical bundle_id, and post-claim republish claimable=false with identical bundle_id; a second distinct sender reports exactly PREKEY_BUNDLE_UNAVAILABLE at exit 3, while an untrusted sender still reports CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED at exit 3, so the two are distinguishable; and a publish response with claimable deleted by a mutating loopback proxy is refused rather than reported as success. E2E evidence is completely unfiltered: 24 of 24 two-process iterations clean across eight complete executions, plus 7 green runs of the new publication-claimability e2e suite. Go: untagged, untagged -race -count=1, and relayv2 -race -count=1 all exit 0; the verbose relayv2 run records 39 top-level tests, 39 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, 0 data races. Test integrity: 46 test files and 5 key config files SHA-256 verified unchanged before and after (46 OK / 0 FAILED, 5 OK / 0 FAILED); 0 skip/only/todo/t.Skip matches workspace-wide. Reconciliation against the 128 recorded at the previous T42 attempt: now 137, +9, entirely in apps/cli (83 to 92), and every one of the +9 is an addition in four new files - relayClient.prekeyUnavailable (+3, T45), relayClient.claimable (+3, T46), cli.relayErrorCodes (+2, T45), e2e/publication-claimability (+1, T44/T45). The five test stubs T46 tightened kept identical test counts and now emit the field the real relay emits, which is a tightening, not a weakening. One INFO finding recorded (T42-I-001): a malformed relay publish response is correctly refused but surfaces as the generic PROTOCOL_REJECTED rather than a distinct malformed-response code. Nothing was modified and nothing committed; the revision identifier is the working tree on unborn main. This gate establishes local technical-prototype behaviour on one macOS arm64 machine only.

acceptance.criterion: Confirm the T45/T46 behaviour holds at the binary level: an exhausted prekey is reported distinguishably from a trust/protocol rejection, and a republish of an already-claimed bundle reports claimable:false, while a genuine trust violation still reports as one.
acceptance.evidence: Binary probe against a freshly built relay and dist/cli.js: publish 1 claimable=true; publish 2 while unclaimed claimable=true, same bundle_id; publish 3 after claim claimable=false, same bundle_id; second distinct trusted sender exit 3 with exactly PREKEY_BUNDLE_UNAVAILABLE (is_CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED=false); untrusted sender exit 3 CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED; codes_distinguishable=true. A mutating loopback proxy deleting claimable from the publish response caused the CLI to refuse the response (exit 3, ok=false) rather than report success, confirming T46 at the binary level.

findings.problem: A malformed relay publish response - specifically one omitting the now-required `claimable` field - is correctly refused by the CLI, but the machine-readable code surfaced to the operator is the generic `PROTOCOL_REJECTED` at exit 3, not a code that names a malformed relay response. The transport raises its own `INVALID_RELAY_RESPONSE` (apps/cli/src/transport/relayClient.ts:20), which `classify()` in apps/cli/src/commands/cli.ts flattens because `reportedRelayCodes` enumerates relay-chosen codes only.
findings.impact: Diagnostic only; the refusal itself is correct and T46's requirement is met. The operator is told the relay rejected the request when in fact the relay's answer was malformed - the same shape of misreporting that T44/T45 fixed one layer in, for the exhausted-prekey case. No requirement currently names a code for this condition and no test asserts one, so this is an observation for the orchestrator rather than a gate failure.
findings.suggested_fix: If the flow's documentation task enumerates operator-facing CLI error codes, consider whether a malformed relay response deserves its own code alongside PREKEY_BUNDLE_UNAVAILABLE, or record deliberately that it does not. No code change is proposed by this verification.
findings.evidence: Binary probe via a mutating loopback proxy that deleted `claimable` from the /v2/prekeys/publish response: erin_via_proxy_claimable_stripped exit=3 ok=false code=PROTOCOL_REJECTED, versus the pass-through control exit=0 ok=true claimable=true.
